summary.text: Josh Kaul is the incumbent Democratic Attorney General of Wisconsin, seeking a third term in a rematch with Republican Eric Toney, whom he narrowly defeated in 2022. A former federal prosecutor, he took office in January 2019. His campaign centers on public safety; his office has also joined more than 60 lawsuits against the Trump administration and brought the suit over Wisconsin's 1849 abortion law.

paragraphs.text: Josh Kaul grew up in Oshkosh and Fond du Lac and graduated from Fond du Lac High School.

He earned a bachelor's degree in economics and history from Yale University in 2003 and a law degree from Stanford Law School in 2006, where he was president of the law review, and then clerked for U.S. Circuit Judge Michael Boudin.
Kaul worked at the law firm Jenner & Block from 2007 to 2010, and from 2010 to 2014 he was an assistant U.S. attorney in the District of Maryland.
In 2014 he joined Perkins Coie as a voting rights attorney.
Kaul was sworn in as Wisconsin's 45th Attorney General on January 7, 2019, and PBS Wisconsin reports that he has won twice by less than a percentage point.
He advanced from the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary, and his campaign describes him as a father, a husband and a former federal prosecutor.
